I'm 49 years old, been farming these 200 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. Middle school education — I can read fertilizer labels and do basic cost calculations, but honestly most of what I know comes from walking these fields every season and watching what happens. My wife and I are the only ones at home now; our kids work in the city. So running 200 mu means I rely on machinery and hired labor. I own a rotary tiller and planter, and I hire a combine for harvest.

My backbone is wheat-maize double cropping on 150 mu. That's the system I trust. I plant wheat in the first week of October with an improved variety — about 60 yuan per mu for seed. I put down basal compound fertilizer at sowing, roughly 80 jin per mu of 15-15-15. Then in March, at jointing, I topdress with urea — about 40 jin per mu. That works out to about 19 kg of pure nitrogen per mu, plus 11 kg of P₂O₅ and 5 kg of K₂O from the compound. I irrigate four times: winter irrigation after sowing, then green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Each irrigation costs about 50 yuan per mu in electricity, so water is a real expense, but without it the yield drops too much. Last year I got about 1,100 jin per mu and I'm hoping for about the same — roughly 550 kg per mu.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, usually mid-June. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days — so I hire the combine and plant the same day, mostly no-till. I use hybrid seed, about 55 yuan per mu. Basal compound goes down with the planter, about 100 jin per mu, and I do one topdressing at the big flare stage if the plants look light-colored. That's about 13 kg pure nitrogen per mu, plus 4 kg each of P₂O₅ and K₂O. I irrigate twice — at big flare and grain filling. Maize usually gives me about 1,200 jin per mu, so around 600 kg.

I put 30 mu into cabbage because when the price is right, it pays better than grain. I plant in mid-March with an improved variety. Cabbage needs more care — rotary tillage first, then bed preparation. I apply basal compound and topdress at rosette stage. Total about 24 kg pure nitrogen per mu, plus 12 kg P₂O₅ and 12 kg K₂O. It needs water more often too — five irrigations through the season. The main problem is cabbage worms, so I spray insecticide and fungicide regularly, plus herbicide. Yield should be around 8,000 jin per mu, which is 4,000 kg. But it eats up hired labor — about 40 days just for cabbage.

The remaining 20 mu I plant millet in late June. Millet is my low-risk crop — drought tolerant, doesn't need much. I rotary till and put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer at sowing, about 10 kg pure nitrogen per mu and 6 kg each of P₂O₅ and K₂O. One irrigation is usually enough. I get about 700 jin per mu, 350 kg. Not big money, but it breaks the rotation and the price is steady.

Total input costs run me about 180,000 yuan for the year. That's a lot of cash to put out before I see any income, but I've learned that cutting back on fertilizer or irrigation costs more in lost yield than it saves. The main constraint is labor — with just two of us, I have to hire for cabbage transplanting, wheat harvest, and any heavy work. Machinery saves me on wheat and maize, but vegetables still need hands.
